# Gas mixture conductivity by Mason-Saxena mixing over Chung pure-component conductivities

`eos.mason_saxena_conductivity`

## Source

**Mason, E. A.; Saxena, S. C. (1958); Chung et al. (1988)**

Mason-Saxena mixing is Mason & Saxena, Physics of Fluids 1(5), 361-369; the pure-component conductivity it mixes is Chung et al., Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 27(4), 671-679.

DOI: [10.1063/1.1724352](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1724352)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Cv0` | J/(mol*K) | ideal-gas heat capacity at constant volume of each component at `T` |
| `M` | kg/mol | molar mass of each component |
| `omega` | dimensionless | acentric factor of each component |
| `Tc` | K | critical temperature of each component |
| `Vc` | m**3/mol | critical volume of each component |
| `dipole` | dimensionless | dipole moment of each component, in debye |
| `kappa` | dimensionless | viscosity correction factor of each component |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `z` | dimensionless | mole fractions; non-negative and summing to one. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `k` | W/(m*K) | the gas mixture thermal conductivity |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- the per-component constants are those of the gas components intended, and the caller resolved them from the databank by name - this model takes the numbers, not the names.

- each pure-component conductivity is `eos.chung_conductivity`'s at the mixture temperature, which is what NeqSim's `ChungConductivityMethod.calcConductivity` does.

- the pure-component conductivity is the *dilute-gas* correlation, so it carries no density dependence and the model takes no molar volume.

- `z` is checked (non-negative, sums to one) rather than renormalised, so a composition error is a loud failure, not a silently different fluid.

- the correlation is for a gas; the dilute-gas form stops being valid into the liquid region.

## References

- Mason, E. A.; Saxena, S. C. (1958). "Approximate formula for the thermal conductivity of gas mixtures." Physics of Fluids 1(5), 361-369. DOI 10.1063/1.1724352.
- Chung, T.-H.; Ajlan, M.; Lee, L. L.; Starling, K. E. (1988). "Generalized multiparameter correlation for nonpolar and polar fluid transport properties." Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 27(4), 671-679. DOI 10.1021/ie00076a024.
